ordered_diagnoses: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s with recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
presented with a pruritic rash ongoing for 2 weeks
The rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
then gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
She denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Erythematous annular plaques without scale on her right arm and bilateral legs
4-mm punch biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain was negative for fungal organisms
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating numerous scattered eosinophils

concepts.why: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale are consistent with eosinophilic dermatitis.
The patient's recent initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen and the development of a pruritic rash are consistent with an immune-related adverse event of immunotherapy.
The patient's use of pembrolizumab and the development of a pruritic rash are consistent with a pembrolizumab-induced rash.
The patient's use of ipilimumab and the development of a pruritic rash are consistent with an ipilimumab-induced rash.

concepts.preferred_label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
concepts.why: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale are consistent with DRESS syndrome, although the lack of systemic symptoms makes this diagnosis less likely.

The presence of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils, as well as the negative PAS stain for fungal organisms, points to eosinophilic cellulitis as a possible diagnosis.

rationales.F02: The patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, which increases the likelihood of an immune-related adverse event (irAE).
rationales.F08: The presence of erythematous annular plaques without scale is consistent with a rash, which could be related to the patient's immunotherapy regimen.
rationales.F09: The biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils are consistent with eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F10: The negative PAS stain rules out a fungal infection, making DRESS syndrome less likely.
rationales.F12: The presence of numerous scattered eosinophils on hematoxylin and eosin stain is consistent with eosinophilic dermatitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the lack of systemic symptoms make Eosinophilic dermatitis the most specific diagnosis, while irAE is a broader category that is also supported by the patient's immunotherapy regimen and rash onset.
